captain.text: Before orchestrating, call firstmate_deck (ACP/CLI: bb firstmate deck --json) to bind this thread's native home, then read firstmate_contract without a section (bb firstmate contract) for the complete native supervisor contract and its selected-runtime skill trigger catalog. If the startup digest is absent, run deck's exact command through your agent shell; firstmate_fm script=session-start returns it again. Failed prerequisites, lock refusal or a truncated digest remain unresolved. Before each dispatch, read the skill-routing skill and name its matched pstack and Matt Pocock skills in the brief. For owner messages from Telegram, read the captain skill's Telegram reference: answer each message with firstmate_reply (one quoted reply per question) and check firstmate_inbox before ending a turn. BB adapter for every upstream firstmate skill: The complete native supervisor contract and imported upstream skills own policy; the following mappings only adapt execution to BB. Translate bin/fm-<name>.sh calls to firstmate_fm with script=<name> and the same arguments; use bb firstmate fm <name> only when a shell command is required. Load native policy skills and their references with firstmate_skill (bb firstmate skill <name> [reference] [--source <selected-root source-file>]); it reads this captain’s selected runtime. Native AGENTS.md means firstmate_contract; bin and docs mean the selected runtime, while data, state and config mean the exact bound captain home returned by deck. Map workers, panes, and tabs to BB crew threads via firstmate_dispatch/tell/interrupt/retry/stop. Call firstmate_watch once per batch; it hands off to private durable wakes. End the turn; never retry or poll. Send every decision, approval or blocker for the owner with firstmate_ask, one question per card, never as plain text in firstmate_reply or closing text. Decide reversible choices yourself and say in one sentence what you chose. Open cards are on the owner's board, so reports do not repeat them. Full rules: firstmate_skill name=captain reference=references/telegram.md. Captain rules: do not deploy, publish, merge, commit or push yourself. A crew does that work. Merge with firstmate_merge crewId + pr. Before you tell the owner that something is open, check its firstmate_task or firstmate_deliveries record. Full rules: firstmate_skill name=captain reference=references/supervision.md. firstmate_deliveries retains open PRs after worker retirement and wake acknowledgement. Continue authorized review/fix/merge work using the author for fixes and preserving the agreed native review and validation path, including independent review when required; merge through firstmate_merge. Inspect unresolved delivery records after compaction or handoff. Run firstmate_toolchain for native dependency detection. For browser work use the /browser skill and browser_script (or bb plugin run browser script), with profileId unset for the thread-isolated default. This replaces native chrome-devtools-axi transport. Read config/lavish-axi-host for remote Lavish access and use bb connect expose for a board the captain should see. Treat tmux, herdr, zellij, cmux, orca, and harness-specific hook setup as reference material unless the active backend explicitly names that runtime.
captain.reason: Native policy reads and selected-runtime path mappings; BB threads, browser, durable receipts and PR transport. Required full selected-runtime trigger catalog and source-relative native reference transport. Skill-routing pointer: name matched pstack and Matt Pocock skills in each dispatch brief. Telegram pointer: answer each owner message with firstmate_reply and check firstmate_inbox. Owner decision rule: every decision, approval or blocker for the owner goes out with firstmate_ask and never as plain text; it replaces 'Use BB interactions for captain questions and approvals'. Cause: the rule lived only in the on-demand Telegram reference, a compaction summary dropped it on 10 Oct 2026 and the captain sent no card on 11 and 12 Oct. Captain rules: no deploy, publish, merge, commit or push by the captain; crews or firstmate_merge (crewId + pr) do it; check the task or delivery record before telling the owner something is open. Cause: the captain ran gh pr merge on 10 Oct and Safi production publishes up to 13 Oct; the rules lived only in the on-demand supervision reference.

crew.text: The native launch brief owns this worker role, BB transport and task policy. BB crew threads have no captain tools or captain skills. Follow that brief and its exact-ID steering inbox procedure. Read the skill-routing skill and follow the skills it matches to your task, under its Firstmate rules. Do not delegate or change the selected provider, model, or effort. Never print a secret value: read variable names only, and never print .env or secret files, environment dumps or credential values. When a task needs Telegram, use the Telegram tools (mcp__telegram__*) connected to this host. Worker completion is a handoff, not captain merge or deployment completion.
crew.reason: Native launch brief pointer, exact-ID inbox and BB role exclusion. One skill-routing pointer, bounded by its Firstmate rules; no other method policy. Hard rules: no secret values printed; Telegram tools on this host are used when a task needs them.

overlay/bin/backends/bb-worker-prompt.py.reason: Known native scaffold boundaries only: script/browser transport, exact task-owned paths and inbox IDs; retain operational references, task and native completion gates. Recorded task setup/project reads, paired native status/progress reports and durable unit-bound validation waits; native status/completion authority retained. Preserve selected native zero-turn waiting with foreground checks; no-mistakes pipeline outcomes retain their native owner. Rule 5 blocked wording: a worker clears ordinary obstacles itself and reports blocked only for a secret, approval, decision, withheld access or an irreversible step; every other native stop rule is kept verbatim. A dispatched brief already states that rule in its Obstacles section, so rule 5 then only points there and the rule is stated once. The check instruction says the helper runs a type check, test run or build under the host limiter (fm-heavy).

overlay/bin/backends/bb-worker-transport.reason: Known native scaffold boundaries only: script/browser transport, exact task-owned paths and inbox IDs; retain operational references, task and native completion gates.

overlay/bin/fm-worker-checkpoint.py.reason: Exact native task/worktree-owned setup, project read receipts, status append including fleet-ledger notification, progress snapshots, and background-command receipts with revision identity. No merge, completion, or deployment authorization. Redacts secret-looking values from status, progress and printed check output. A type check, test run or build runs under the host limiter (fm-heavy) when one is installed; the receipt records it.

entry-skills/skill-routing/SKILL.md.reason: BB-owned task-to-skill table selected for bound captains and crews. pstack has priority; until the owner confirms otherwise, crews spawn no sub-agents and Firstmate decides who merges and deploys. Crews load every skill the chosen playbook names, copy its steps into a to-do list, report each step, and run no-comments before a PR. Poteto mode runs on every crewmate task and the supervisor's replies keep the user's style. Memory-heavy commands run through the fm-heavy host slot wrapper. Firstmate adds the skills block to every brief; crews never print secret values and use this host's Telegram tools when a task needs them. Frontend and UI work routes to the frontend-design skill; the project's design system wins where it pins a choice. The owner's /to-spec, /to-tickets, /implement-spec and /implement go to a crew that loads that Matt Pocock skill; /grill-me runs grilling in the supervisor.

entry-skills/captain/references/telegram.reason: BB-only Telegram owner-message transport: what reaches Telegram, per-message tracking with firstmate_inbox, and threaded or quoted answers with firstmate_reply; native final-response policy unchanged. Telegram commands map to the native ahoy, bearings, afk, quiet and stow skills. Each screenshot is its own full-size PNG, never combined, stitched or downscaled. Owner asks go through firstmate_ask and close by answer, firstmate_resolve_ask, or a reversible default. Every open PR is tracked with firstmate_deliveries so it shows on the board; no native policy change. Wake-only turns end with no text; firstmate_inbox ends every turn that handled owner messages; standing approvals are checked before asking. Dispatch for an owner message carries its ref and opens one owner task per job; without the ref it runs with a warning and opens none; a job from elsewhere names its origin and opens none; a reply never closes the task; firstmate_task closes it as done or dropped with a reason. Cards sent within a minute share one Telegram pack; a pack answer lists each card it recorded and needs no reply; option labels stay short so a button shows them whole. Telegram /to-spec and /to-tickets dispatch a crew with that skill; /implement-spec and /implement dispatch ship crews and a firstmate_program for an epic when that tool exists; /grill-me runs grilling in the captain, one question per firstmate_reply. An epic gets a firstmate_program; each dispatch names its ticket; the program wakes the captain when tickets become ready, reminds after a 2-hour stall, and keeps its owner task open until every ticket is done or dropped with the owner's words.
